chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Hajjaj from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Hamzah ibn Humran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A faqih (jurist) never repeats the prayer unless he plans for it and manages it so that he does not have to repeat it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is specific to certain rulings, because we have clarified that in forgetfulness there is that which cannot be compensated for, and in it only the repetition of the prayer is permissible.

key_terms.السَّهْو: Forgetfulness or inadvertent error in prayer
key_terms.فَقِي: Jurist or scholar of Islamic law
key_terms.يَحْتَالُ: To plan or devise a strategy

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeating prayer due to forgetfulness according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the ideal of *itqan* (perfection) in prayer, urging the *faqih* to deliberate and structure his worship to avoid errors requiring repetition. Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentator clarifies that this is not an absolute prohibition against re-praying, but rather a directive to minimize unnecessary repetition by addressing specific types of forgetfulness where the error is irremediable through standard corrective actions like *sajdah al-sahw*.
